title: Metronomad Phase 6 — Beat Dots, Progress, Clock Hygiene via TDD (B-01…B-05 + wiring, D9/U-17/U-22)
outcome: Phase 6 (Beat Dots, Progress, Clock Hygiene, P1) automated criteria complete. RED-GREEN-REFACTOR in 6 small batches: B-01 dot rendering (RAF callback-collector, 4 tests incl. lead-in + grid-null loop self-termination) → B-02 visibilitychange pause/snap/resume (2 tests) → B-03 reduced-motion static highlight + live media change + --beat-interval tempo sync (4 tests) → B-04 progress computeds characterization (2 tests, green immediately — Phase 5 code) → B-05 stopAll teardown (1 test: RAF cancel + engine.dispose watch-interval spy + matchMedia listener removal + idempotency) → Phase-6 wiring in UiHandlersTest (4 tests: countingIn starts the clock exactly once, playing flip does not restart, all three terminal states stop, onVisibilityChange delegates, no-_beatDots safety). Final: BeatDots 14/14, full unit suite 127/127 (5 files), E2E smoke 4/4, live page mounts with zero console errors and beatDot-0..3 ids present. REFACTOR: extracted _cancelLoop() (single RAF-teardown point), _render() now returns the grid so _tick/_renderNow stop double-calling engine.getBeatGrid(), single _dotEls() lookup per frame; the refactor initially broke B-02 (_cancelLoop reset _hiddenPaused that the hidden path had just set) — caught by the suite, fixed by keeping the helper side-effect-free. Production: createBeatDots.js (RAF visualizer, D9 pure phase per frame, imperative dot classes, tenth-second-throttled songPosition), methods (_startBeatDots/_stopBeatDots/onVisibilityChange + onEngineStateChange hooks), lifecycle (createBeatDots + document visibilitychange listener in mounted; stopAll first in beforeUnmount), template (dot ids, imperative --active ownership documented), Style.css (pulse on --active.--pulse at --beat-interval, --static variant, media-query safety net), barrel export. Manual gate remains: U-17 (tab switch snap), U-22 (reduced motion), dot/click lockstep at 120 & 250 BPM — phase map left 'in progress' until the user verifies.
key_decisions: createBeatDots owns the APP-LEVEL RAF loop (window.requestAnimationFrame, collector-mockable per B-01) instead of reusing the engine's P-12 visual clock: the app loop needs visibility-pause, tempo-driven CSS (--beat-interval), and reduced-motion class switching, none of which are engine concerns. The engine's startVisualClock/onFrame remains a tested public capability (P-12) but is unused by the app — noted, not deleted (removing tested Phase-4 surface mid-plan is out of scope)

Dot classes are owned IMPERATIVELY by createBeatDots (classList --active/--pulse/--static); the template keeps only the static downbeat modifier plus the :data-beat row hook (KB-6). Rationale: BeatDotsTest.html has no Vue mount, so B-01's DOM-class assertions require imperative ownership; a Vue :class binding on the same attribute would clobber per-frame writes on re-render
vm.activeBeatIndex stores the DOWNSAMPLED dot index (beatIndex % 4, or -1), not the absolute beat — it drives the data-beat E2E hook which must match the lit dot (0-3)

stopAll(vm) calls getEngine().dispose(): B-05 requires stopAll to cancel the D10 watch interval, which only engine.dispose() clears; beforeUnmount therefore does stopAll (RAF + media listener + engine) → fileLoader.release(), with a defensive engine.dispose fallback if _beatDots is absent. stopAll is idempotent via a _stopped flag (double unmount must not dispose twice)

The visual clock runs for the count-in/song SEQUENCE only: starts on 'countingIn' (idempotent), keeps running through the countingIn→playing flip (one sequence, one loop — the downbeat is on the same grid, D9), stops on stopped/ended/previewEnded. Preview runs no loop (getBeatGrid is null there); U-09's 'progress reset to the offset' is satisfied by _returnToReady

Progress readout sync is throttled to tenth-second changes (compare formatTime output before writing vm.songPosition) per the plan's per-frame performance note; --beat-interval is set on the dot row from grid.interval so the CSS pulse runs at the song's beat rate (0.5s at 120 BPM, 0.24s at 250)

Reduced motion (B-03/U-22): JS reads matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') — active dot gets beat-dot--static (no --pulse) and a 'change' listener applies the swap LIVE without a new frame; the CSS media query remains as the no-JS safety net. matchMedia is NOT injected (base = getEngine/getClock/getDom per the pinned interface) — tests stub window.matchMedia and restore in afterEach

Test clock values were pinned to the T-08 corrected input (101.75 → {beatIndex: 2, inBeat: 0.5} on a 100.5/0.5 grid) after the first GREEN attempt exposed an arithmetic slip (102.75 is beat 4.5); a separate bar-wrap test locks in the modulo (absolute beat 4 → dot 0)
learnings: The RAF callback-collector mock MUST be browser-faithful about cancellation: the first version only recorded canceled ids and left the callback queued, so 'cancel then assert nothing pending' silently failed with a phantom pending frame. Model pending frames as a Map id→cb and DELETE on cancel (same shape as PlaybackEngineTest's createFakeRAF)

Refactor regression caught by the suite (Critical, fixed): extracting _cancelLoop() from stopVisualClock/onVisibilityChange/stopAll and giving it _hiddenPaused = false wiped the flag the hidden branch set immediately before calling it — B-02's visible-resume stopped working. When extracting a helper from call sites that write state AROUND the call, audit each flag: the helper should have the minimal side effects all callers share

document.hidden is testable in the real browser via Object.defineProperty(document, 'hidden', {configurable: true, get: () => value}) with the original Document.prototype descriptor saved and restored in afterEach — no framework needed

A phase's own test page can double as the home for characterization tests of adjacent computeds: B-04 (progress fill/marker/aria-label) asserts Phase-5 computeds from createMetronomadApp, keeping the phase file's 'BeatDotsTest covers B-01…B-05' contract true while avoiding cross-page duplication of the appOptions-capture boilerplate

Imperative DOM ownership vs Vue bindings is a per-attribute decision: the attribute the RAF writes (--active class) must be unbound in the template, while attributes Vue owns (data-beat, progress :style/:aria-label) stay bound and are fed through vm data — mixing the two on one attribute causes silent clobbering on the next patch
